bantu-expansion.name: Bantu expansion
bantu-expansion.summary: A series of prehistoric migrations, roughly 4000 BCE to 500 CE, of Bantu-speaking peoples from West-Central Africa across Central, Eastern and Southern Africa.

african-pygmies.name: African Pygmies
african-pygmies.summary: Central African ethnic groups, including the Mbenga, Mbuti and Twa, traditionally living by foraging and hunting in the Congo Basin, descended from the region's earliest Middle Stone Age inhabitants.

shum-laka.name: Shum Laka
shum-laka.summary: Rockshelter archaeological site in the Grasslands region of northwest Cameroon, occupied during the Later Stone Age, important for studying the spread of Bantu-speaking peoples.

elam.name: Elam
elam.summary: An ancient civilization centered in western and southwestern Iran, one of the leading political forces of the ancient Near East, with written records from around 3000 BCE.

elmenteitan.name: Elmenteitan
elmenteitan.summary: A prehistoric stone-tool and pottery tradition of pastoralist herders on Kenya's western plains around 3300 to 1200 years ago, named after nearby Lake Elmenteita.

hanno-the-navigator.name: Hanno the Navigator
hanno-the-navigator.summary: A Carthaginian explorer of the 5th century BC known for a naval expedition along West Africa's coast, described in an account (periplus) that may show him reaching as far as modern Gabon.

incense-trade-route.name: Incense trade route
incense-trade-route.summary: Ancient network of land and sea trade routes linking the Mediterranean with sources of incense, spices, and luxury goods, flourishing from about the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.

three-age-system.name: Three-age system
three-age-system.summary: A 19th-century method of ordering prehistoric artifacts and periods into a Stone Age, Bronze Age and Iron Age, still central to European and Near Eastern archaeology.

lejja.name: Lejja
lejja.summary: A community of 33 villages in southeastern Nigeria with iron-smelting evidence dating to 2000 BC, among the earliest known ironworking sites in sub-Saharan Africa.

khoisan.name: Khoisan
khoisan.summary: An umbrella term for Southern Africa's non-Bantu indigenous peoples, combining the Khoekhoen and Sān, who speak click languages and descend from some of the earliest modern human populations in the region.

african-great-lakes.name: African Great Lakes
african-great-lakes.summary: A group of Rift Valley lakes in East Africa, including Lake Victoria and Lake Tanganyika, holding about a quarter of the world's unfrozen fresh water and exceptional fish biodiversity.
